app.name: paperpack
app.privacy: Everything is worked out inside this browser. Nothing you type is sent anywhere.
app.tagline: Work out your Australian working holiday tax refund and your departing super, before you claim either one yourself.
disclaimer.body: This is a calculator, not a tax agent. It is not a registered tax agent service and nothing here is tax advice. Every figure is an estimate based on published ATO rates applied to what you typed. Check it against your own records, and if you need advice you can rely on, ask a registered tax agent.
disclaimer.confirm: I have checked these figures against my own records and understand they are an estimate.
disclaimer.effective: Rates effective {from}, last checked against the source on {checked}.
disclaimer.title: Read this before you use any number below
flag.deductions-need-written-evidence: Above 300 dollars in total work expenses you need written evidence for all of it, not just the part above 300.
flag.lodging-is-optional-but-refund-need: On working holiday wages under 45,001 dollars you are not required to lodge. But a refund only arrives if you do.
flag.medicare-entitlement-statement-may-: If you were not entitled to Medicare, an entitlement statement from Services Australia may remove this levy.
flag.medicare-exemption-claimed: The levy is left out because you said you hold an entitlement statement.
flag.no-tfn-withholding-is-recoverable: Tax withheld at 45 per cent because no tax file number was given is not lost. Lodging is how you get it back.
flag.resident-but-whm-rates-still-apply: Answering that you were a resident does not change your rate. Working holiday rates apply regardless of residency unless you hold the passport of one of eight treaty countries.
flag.rhca-country-medicare-likely-payabl: Your country has a reciprocal health care agreement with Australia. Whether it actually covers you turns on health insurance or on where you lived before arriving, not on your passport, and if it covers you then a resident usually pays the levy. Italian and Maltese cover runs out after six months, which is shorter than the visa.
help.daysInAustralia: Being here more than half the year is one of the residency tests, but it is not the only one and it does not settle the question by itself.
help.grossIncome: Add up every income statement in myGov, plus any cash work. Cash counts.
help.hasMedicareEntitlementStatement: It comes from Services Australia and you can apply from 1 July. Apply before you lodge, not after. If you are leaving Australia you can apply up to four weeks before you go, and it is processed after you leave.
help.isAustralianTaxResident: This is your call, not ours. The ATO says most working holiday visa holders are not residents. Read the residency tests on the ATO site and answer for your own situation.
help.nationality: Nationality changes the answer for a small number of countries, because of tax treaty and health care agreements.
help.providedTfn: Without one, tax is withheld at 45 per cent. You get the excess back when you lodge.
help.taxWithheld: Also on your income statements. If an employer withheld too much, this is where the refund comes from.
help.workRelatedDeductions: Protective boots, hi vis, sunscreen for outdoor work, laundry of work clothing, tools, travel between two jobs on the same day. Not your commute, not your visa fee, not ordinary clothes.

q.residentMonths: How many months of the year were you an Australian resident for tax purposes?
help.residentMonths: Count the month you arrived as a whole month, through to 30 June. Arriving on 3 January and arriving on 31 January both count as six months. Answer 12 if you were a resident for the whole year.
flag.nda-resident-basis-is-lower: You are taxed on whichever of two bases costs less. Being assessed like a resident Australian national on the same income comes out cheaper here, so that is what this uses.
flag.nda-whm-basis-is-lower: You are taxed on whichever of two bases costs less, and here that is the working holiday maker basis, so the treaty makes no difference to what you pay.
flag.foreign-income-changes-the-comparis: This assumes everything you earned was earned in Australia. Interest, dividends or wages from home count on the resident side of the comparison but not the working holiday side, which can flip which side is cheaper. If you had any, do not rely on this figure.
flag.part-year-threshold-applied: You were a resident for part of the year, so your tax free threshold is smaller than the full 18,200 dollars. Staying until 30 June does not avoid this.
flag.below-the-medicare-levy-threshold: Your income is under the Medicare levy threshold, so no levy is included.
flag.medicare-thresholds-not-published-f: The Medicare levy thresholds for this year have not been published yet, so a resident’s tax cannot be worked out here. They usually appear early in the calendar year after the income year ends.
result.comparison: The treaty gives you the lower of these two
result.whmBasis: Assessed as a working holiday maker
flag.every-deduction-needs-written-evide: From this year the 300 dollar no receipts allowance is gone. Every dollar of work expense you claim needs written evidence.
flag.standard-deduction-applied: A standard deduction of up to 1,000 dollars for work expenses has been applied because you were a resident. It replaces your own claim rather than adding to it, so claiming more than 1,000 dollars in real expenses is worth more.
disclaimer.checked: Rates last checked against the source on {checked}.
q.superBalance: How much super is in your fund, before tax?
help.superBalance: The balance the fund will pay out. Your fund app or last statement has it. If you had several jobs you may have several funds, so add them up or work them out one at a time.
q.everHeldWhmVisa: Have you ever held a 417 or 462 visa?
help.everHeldWhmVisa: Working Holiday (417) or Work and Holiday (462) at any point, along with any bridging visa attached to one. How long ago does not matter.
q.superFromWhmPeriod: Does this super include anything paid in while you held that visa?
help.superFromWhmPeriod: This is the part people get wrong. Holding the visa is not enough on its own. If even part of the balance went in during that time, the higher rate takes the whole payment. If none of it did, the ordinary rates apply.
q.taxFreeComponent: How much of the balance is a tax free component?
help.taxFreeComponent: Usually nothing. It comes from money you paid in yourself after tax, not from what an employer paid. Your fund statement names it. Enter 0 if none of it came out of your own pocket.
q.untaxedElement: How much of it is an untaxed element?
help.untaxedElement: Almost always nothing. It comes from unfunded public sector schemes rather than ordinary industry or retail funds. Your fund statement names it. Enter 0 if it does not appear there.
q.visaCeased: Has your visa expired or been cancelled?
help.visaCeased: A fund cannot pay you out while the visa is still active.
help.hasDeparted: You can fill the application in before you go, but the payment only happens once you have left.
dasp.tax: Tax taken out of the payment
flag.whm-rate-covers-the-whole-payment: Because part of this super went in while you held a working holiday visa, 65 per cent applies to the whole payment. It is not split between visas and there is no apportioning.
flag.ordinary-rates-despite-having-held-: You held a working holiday visa, but you said none of this super went in during that time, so the ordinary rates apply instead of 65 per cent. Check your contribution history before you rely on that.
flag.nothing-is-payable-until-the-visa-e: Two things have to be true before a fund pays anything out: the visa has ended, and you have left Australia. The figure above is what it would come to when they are.
flag.components-add-up-to-more-than-the-: The components you entered come to more than the balance, so the figures above are wrong. Check them against your fund statement.
